text: Which of these is a *consequence* of erasure rather than an independent design choice?
choices: A class may implement many interfaces but extend only one class.
Interfaces may declare `default` methods with bodies.
`ArrayList` grows by roughly half its capacity when it fills.
`List<int>` is illegal, so numbers in collections must be boxed.
explanation: Erasure requires the element to be an `Object` reference, so a primitive cannot be a type argument. That single restriction is why autoboxing exists, why `Stream<Integer>` measured ten times slower than `IntStream` in Chapter 26, and why `java.util.function` needs forty interfaces instead of six. Chapter 16 introduced the primitive/object split as a 1995 decision; this is where the bill arrives.
